Class Button

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.AbstractPanelElement
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.Button
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
public class Button extends AbstractPanelElement
An interactive button within a Panel: a raised background with a centred label, an icon, or a consumer sprite as its whole face. 
Button.builder()
        .label(Component.literal("Sort"))
        .at(0, 0).size(60, 16)
        .onClick(this::sort)
        .tooltip(Component.literal("Sort this container"))
        .build();

Three faces, one builder

  • Label (default): label(text). A width of 0 sizes the button to its label. When the panel narrows it below the label, the label wraps and the button grows taller.
  • Icon: icon(sprite), a square button with the sprite inset 2px so the bevel shows; dimmed while disabled. Pair it with a tooltip.
  • Sprite: sprite(sprite), the sprite is the whole button (frame included); pressed draws it with its lightness inverted, hovered adds a highlight, disabled a dark overlay. A label, if given, sits on top.

Input

Left click runs onClick and plays vanilla's click sound. Other buttons reach onSecondaryClick when one is set (it gets a Click with the modifier keys), else fall through to vanilla. Keyboard: Tab focuses the button and Enter or Space presses it, through the shared ElementWidget, which also gives it narration. Disabled (its own disabledWhen, or its panel's) it draws greyed and takes nothing.

Extension points for consumer subclasses

A subclass (Keybindery's chord face is one) builds through Button(Builder) and overrides renderBackground(RenderContext, int, int, Button.Look) and renderContent(RenderContext, int, int, Button.Look), which receive this frame's Button.Look. The orchestrating render(RenderContext) is final.

    • isInteractive

      public boolean isInteractive()
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Whether this element handles pointer input, so a point on it is a solid claim on a transparent panel. Controls return true; render-only decorations keep the false default, so they never eat a click they do nothing with.

    • render

      public final void render(RenderContext ctx)
      Resolves this frame's look (hovered, pressed, disabled), paints background, tint and content through the hooks, keeps the vanilla widget current, and queues the tooltip. Final: the extension surface is the two hooks.

    • renderBackground

      protected void renderBackground(RenderContext ctx, int sx, int sy, Button.Look look)
      Paints the background: raised, inset while pressed, dark while disabled, with the hover highlight; or vanilla's button sprite under ControlStyle.VANILLA. Covers the grown height when the label wraps.

      Stable extension point. sx/sy are the button's screen-space top-left; runs before renderContent(RenderContext, int, int, Button.Look); must not mutate the button.

    • renderContent

      protected void renderContent(RenderContext ctx, int sx, int sy, Button.Look look)

      Stable extension point. sx/sy are the button's screen-space top-left; runs after renderBackground(RenderContext, int, int, Button.Look); must not mutate the button.
